title: Ordered finite-field models and filtration for norm-continuous constructible modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put
$$C(S)=\{f\in C(S,\Omega):f(S)\subset E\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset\Omega\},\quad B(S)=C(S,\Omega),\quad A_E(S)=C(S,E).$$
Use the condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], their coefficient pullbacks $R_T=p_T^*R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(R_T)$ of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Constructible always means finite constant local models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and lisse means finite free on a pro-étale cover [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ define $a_!=i_*j_!$ for an open-then-closed factorization $a=i\circ j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star].

Let $M$ be a constructible $B_X$-module. Suppose given a finite constructible locally closed scheme partition $X=\coprod_a S_a$, finite intermediate fields $E_a\subset\Omega$, lisse $A_{E_a,S_a}$-modules $L_a$, and $B_{S_a}$-linear isomorphisms
$$\phi_a:B_{S_a}\otimes_{A_{E_a,S_a}}L_a\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{S_a}.$$
Write $a_a:S_a\hookrightarrow X$ and $F_a=(a_a)_!L_a$. There is a finite locally closed scheme stratification $X=\coprod_{t=1}^m R_t$ whose successive unions $V_t=\bigcup_{s\le t}|R_s|$ are open ($V_0=\varnothing$, $V_m=X$), together with a choice $a(t)$ for each $t$, such that $|R_t|\subseteq|S_{a(t)}|$ and
$$V'_t=F_{a(t)}|_{R_t}\text{ is lisse over }A_{E_{a(t)},R_t},\qquad
\psi_t:B_{R_t}\otimes_{A_{E_{a(t)},R_t}}V'_t\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{R_t}.$$
The refinement may be chosen adapted to every $F_a$ (each $F_a|_{R_t}$ is lisse over its own coefficient field). Refinement here asserts containment of images, with no assumption that $R_t\to X$ factors through $S_{a(t)}$. In the actual fibre product
$$W_t=R_t\times_X S_{a(t)},\qquad q_t:W_t\to R_t,$$
the map $q_t$ is a surjective closed immersion, and $q_t^*\psi_t$ agrees with the pullback of $\phi_{a(t)}$ under the canonical restriction, scalar and extension-by-zero identifications.

For $v_t:V_t\hookrightarrow X$ and $r_t:R_t\hookrightarrow X$, the open counits give monomorphisms $M_t=(v_t)_!(M|_{V_t})\hookrightarrow M$ and a finite filtration
$$0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_m=M,\qquad
M_t/M_{t-1}\cong(r_t)_!\bigl(B_{R_t}\otimes_{A_{E_{a(t)},R_t}}V'_t\bigr).$$
Each resulting short exact sequence gives the corresponding distinguished triangle of degree-zero objects in $D(B_X)$. The stratification and filtration need not have nonempty strata or strict successive inclusions; empty $X$ and zero $M$ are included.

proof.text: The field k is Noetherian (its only ideals are 0 and k), so the finite-type theorem makes X Noetherian. Apply the locally closed lisse-extension theorem separately to each finite coefficient field E_a and L_a. Normalized factorization independence identifies the supplied extension with the canonical one. It says precisely that F_a=(a_a)_!L_a is constructible in the finite constant scalar-model convention. Choose a finite adapted stratification P_a for each F_a using that definition. There are finitely many P_a even though their coefficient rings differ; the geometric refinement theorem has an unused coefficient parameter.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordered finite-model obligation; generation converse in sk-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation.proof.md

proof.text: Apply the common-refinement theorem to the given partition (S_a) and all the P_a simultaneously. Obtain scheme strata R_t with open prefixes V_t, each image contained in some S_a and in a stratum of every P_a. For each a apply clause (2) of the lisse-refinement theorem with coefficient A_{E_a}: it explicitly assumes image containment only and concludes F_a|_{R_t} lisse. Choose a(t) with |R_t| contained in |S_{a(t)}| and put V'_t=F_{a(t)}|_{R_t}. Empty strata can be omitted. For empty X take m=0.

Fix t and write a=a(t), r:R_t->X. Form W=R_t times_X S_a with projections q:W->R_t and b:W->S_a. The base-change immersion theorem makes q an immersion. It is surjective: for x in R_t its image lies in S_a, and the residue-field isomorphism of an immersion at the unique point over that image gives a point of the fibre product over x. Its image is therefore all of R_t, a closed set, so the closed-image immersion theorem makes q a surjective closed immersion. Apply the condensed surjective-closed equivalence with coefficient B. Thus q^* on B-modules is fully faithful and reflects isomorphisms. No factorization of r through S_a has been used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), actual fibre-product correction; Stacks schemes.tex Tags 01JY and 01IQ, proetale.tex Tag 09AB

proof.text: Use the normalized restriction isomorphism a_a^*(a_a)_!L_a -> L_a from locally closed module extension coherence, and inverse-image composition for r q=a_a b. They identify q^*V'_t with b^*L_a. Pullback commutes with ordinary relative scalar extension: its strong monoidal comparison identifies the two arrows defining the relative-tensor coequalizer, and its left-adjoint property preserves that coequalizer. Use the coefficient composition identification to identify q^*B_{R_t}=B_W and q^*A_{E_a,R_t}=A_{E_a,W}. Consequently b^*phi_a defines an isomorphism q^*(B_{R_t} tensor_{A_{E_a,R_t}} V'_t) -> q^*(M|_{R_t}). Full faithfulness in step 3 gives a unique B_{R_t}-linear map psi_t with exactly this pullback. Since q^* reflects isomorphisms, psi_t is invertible. Its defining equation is the requested compatibility, with the normalized extension restriction rather than any unsupported scheme factorization.

source.place: Paragraph (3), descent of the prescribed finite-model isomorphisms; Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09AA, 09AB, 09BN

proof.text: For every open prefix v_t:V_t->X apply the module localization sequence with coefficient B_X to its complementary reduced closed subscheme. It gives a monomorphism epsilon_t:(v_t)_!v_t^*M -> M, namely the specified counit. For W=V_{t-1} inside V_t, the closed-image immersion theorem makes R_t->V_t closed, since its image is V_t minus V_{t-1}. The same localization sequence on V_t gives 0 -> u_!u^*(M|_{V_t}) -> M|_{V_t} -> c_*c^*(M|_{V_t}) -> 0, where u:V_{t-1}->V_t and c:R_t->V_t. All these open immersions are quasi-compact: the locally closed extension theorem includes Noetherianity of these subschemes and quasi-compactness of their opens.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-support filtration; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open)

proof.text: Apply the exact functor (v_t)_! to the sequence in step 5. The normalized composition comparisons identify its first term with M_{t-1} and its last term with (r_t)_!(M|_{R_t}), including the change from closed-then-open to open-then-closed factorization. The first arrow followed by epsilon_t equals epsilon_{t-1}: under the composite open adjunction both maps are the transpose of the identity of M|_{V_{t-1}}. Thus these are inclusions of the same counit subobjects of M, not merely unrelated monomorphisms. Their cokernels give M_t/M_{t-1} isomorphic to (r_t)_!(M|_{R_t}). Apply (r_t)_! to psi_t^{-1} to obtain exactly the displayed quotient with B_{R_t} tensor_{A_{E_{a(t)},R_t}} V'_t. The empty and whole open prefixes give M_0=0 and M_m=M.

source.place: Paragraph (3), exact supported quotient and counit compatibility; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AH

proof.text: Apply the short-exact-sequence derived-triangle theorem in the abelian category of internal B_X-modules to each sequence in step 6. This produces the distinguished triangle of the specified degree-zero objects in the ordinary unbounded derived category. The construction imposes neither strict inclusions nor positive ranks. If M=0 every term and quotient is zero; if X is empty the empty stratification and filtration work.

No E3 factorization is assumed; tested on X=Spec k[ε]/ε² with S=X_red. (4) r_a, pullback composition, the strong-monoidal and left-adjoint abelian pullback preserving the relative-tensor coequalizer, and pullback-from-point-comp give b^*φ_a; full faithfulness and conservativity give ψ_t; the compatibility holds by construction.
